summary: A gi guard companion connecting the course’s double-sleeve control material with lasso/spider defenses and opponent-posture branches.
description: Find a double-sleeve study path that distinguishes obtaining the grips, maintaining control and selecting an attack.
overview: Thomas’s outline crosses several leg configurations while retaining a double-sleeve theme. The useful comparison is between control lessons and the later posture-specific branches, rather than treating every listed sweep as available from one fixed position.

fits: You want to organize gi double-sleeve study around control losses or a standing-to-kneeling posture change.
consider_alternative_if: If your focus is gi single-leg-X entries and fabric-grip sweeps, compare Adam Wardzinski’s guide.

includes: Basic double-sleeve control and De La Riva branches; lasso/spider control and named defenses.
Spider-X material and separate one-knee-up or kneeling-opponent options.
limits: This is a sleeve-based gi approach, and its later leg configurations extend beyond one static double-sleeve position.

start_here.title: Identify control loss before choosing a sweep
start_here.task: Compare the four named lasso/spider defense problems in volume 2 with the one-knee-up and kneeling sections in volume 4. Decide whether the exchange you want to study is a control-loss problem or an attack against a particular posture. Begin with basic control if you cannot yet distinguish the two.
